note: [agent-bulk] shw 13000 (145.1 MeV, 2 seg, len 44.4) is the only shower in this event at or above 20 MeV. It is a single cone: in the az +65 vertex frame its two segments fork out of the region just past the nu vertex star and open away from it, and the pale-yellow halo covers the whole diffuse blob in the az -55 and az +85 frames. The 64.1 deg between its two members is the cone opening as traced by a 2-segment skeleton, NOT two prongs - I checked that on the second azimuth before deciding, and it is why I do not call this over-clustered. Nothing substantial is unclaimed next to it: the only non-members below 40 deg at any distance are 47013 at 14.9 cm / 13.6 deg (kine_best 7.4 MeV, pdg 2212) and 32008 at 26.0 cm / 21.9 deg (2.1 MeV). 47013 is the one thing that could make this under-clustered - it is tier 1 with metric 0.6, BETTER than the shower's own accepted member (metric 1.5) - but it is a 7.4 MeV proton stub sitting off the cone on the vertex side, and leaving a proton out of an EM shower is the right behaviour, so I did not mark it. CAVEAT on my own method here: with only 2 segments, one of them 64 deg off the other, the fitted axis is poorly determined, so the angle-envelope argument I use elsewhere is weak on this event and the verdict rests on the picture - a single covered blob - rather than on the acceptance plot. Topology is other_em single-photon again: a grey unowned track runs to the nu vertex and 13000 is the only EM object; there is no second gamma anywhere, so the absence of a pi0 group is a missing gamma, not a pairing failure. event_flags left empty: a vertex is reconstructed and there is no pi0 to place, so this is not a no-vertex NCpi0. Not looked at: the other 11 showers, all at or below 7.4 MeV (scope rule min_kine_best 20 MeV).
